plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in the southern spring turn lavender-blue as this tree opens its trumpet-shaped flowers in dense clusters. The petals drop to form soft purple carpets beneath the feathery, fern-like canopy.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, peaking from October to December
plants.location: Brisbane and Sydney in Australia, Pretoria in South Africa, and Buenos Aires in Argentina
plants.funFact: The tree is native to South America but is now planted in warm regions worldwide. In Pretoria, which is nicknamed the Jacaranda City, thousands of them line the streets.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub lights up late autumn gardens with delicate, often lightly fragrant blooms. Its flowers are single or semi-double with a golden center of stamens, and they open when most other plants are winding down.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter, roughly October to December
plants.location: Southern Japan, where it is native, and in gardens across the southeastern United States and Europe's mild-climate regions
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Seed from sasanqua and other camellias is pressed to make a culinary and cosmetic oil.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Round umbels of funnel-shaped flowers sway on tall, sturdy stems above arching, strap-like leaves. Each flower head is a burst of blue that looks like a firework.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring through summer in the Southern Hemisphere, starting in November
plants.location: Coastal eastern South Africa, where it grows wild, and gardens across Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Greek words for love and flower. Its thick, water-storing roots help it survive dry spells.
